fields.category: Frank Meyer and early USDA jujube introductions discussed by Yao

rows.name: Chin sze tsao
rows.description: Yao says Frank Meyer sent seed from Chin sze tsao from Shandong Province in 1907 and gives Jinsi zao as the Chinese name

rows.name: Yuen ling tsao
rows.description: Yao says Frank Meyer sent seed from Yuen ling tsao from Shandong Province in 1907 and gives Yuanling zao as the Chinese name

rows.name: Hu ping tsao
rows.description: Yao says Frank Meyer collected Hu ping tsao budwood from Shanxi Province in 1908 and gives Huping zao as the Chinese name

rows.name: Tsui ling tsao
rows.description: Yao says Frank Meyer collected Tsui ling tsao budwood from Shanxi Province in 1908 and gives Cuiling zao as the Chinese name

rows.name: Ta tsao
rows.description: Yao says Meyer collected Ta tsao, but notes that the name means big-fruited tsao and differs from region to region

rows.name: Hsiao tsao
rows.description: Yao says Meyer collected Hsiao tsao, but notes that the name means small-fruited tsao and differs from region to region

rows.name: Wu hu tsao
rows.description: Yao describes Wu hu tsao as a seedless or pitless cultivar collected by Frank Meyer

rows.name: Yu
rows.description: Yao describes Yu as a tooth-shaped jujube cultivar from Frank Meyer's collections and gives Ya zao as the Chinese name

rows.name: So
rows.description: Yao says Frank Meyer collected So, PI 37484, a contorted jujube with gnarled and zigzagged branches

rows.name: Dragon
rows.description: Yao says Frank Meyer collected a jujube with crooked and twisted branches called Dragon or Dragon's-claw

fields.category: USDA Chico jujube recommendations discussed by Yao

rows.name: Mu shing hong
rows.description: Yao says the USDA Chico Station recommended Mu shing hong in the 1920s and described it as one of the best varieties

rows.name: Lang
rows.description: Yao says the USDA Chico Station recommended Lang in the 1920s and described it as the best variety for general purposes

rows.name: Shui men
rows.description: Yao says the USDA Chico Station recommended Shui men in the 1920s and described it as average sized and useful for many purposes

rows.name: Li
rows.description: Yao says the USDA Chico Station recommended Li in the 1920s and described it as having the largest fruit and being one of the best for fresh eating

fields.category: USDA Chico jujube breeding selections discussed by Yao

rows.name: Chico
rows.description: Yao says Chico, also called GI-7-62, was bred at the USDA Chico Station as a seedling of PI 37484, So, and has round but flattened fruit

rows.name: GI-1183
rows.description: Yao says GI-1183 is a jujube cultivar from the USDA Chico Station bred by Ackerman from unknown sources

rows.name: GA866
rows.description: Yao says GA866 was bred and selected at the USDA Chico Station by Ackerman from unknown sources

rows.name: Thornless
rows.description: Yao says Thornless was bred or selected at the USDA Chico Station by Ackerman and Smith, with fruit shape similar to Lang

fields.category: United States jujube selections and recent imports discussed by Yao

rows.name: R3T1
rows.description: Yao says R3T1 was selected from a Tennessee Valley Authority jujube planting near Norris, Tennessee

rows.name: Sherwood
rows.description: Yao says Sherwood was excellent for California, Texas, and Louisiana, but had poor fruit set and did not ripen before first frost in northern New Mexico

rows.name: Autumn Beauty
rows.description: Yao says Jim Gilbert of One Green World Nursery introduced Autumn Beauty from China

rows.name: Winter Delight
rows.description: Yao says Jim Gilbert of One Green World Nursery introduced Winter Delight from China; the source styles the name with a trademark marker
